device.model: uEye camera through the pydcu ctypes wrapper
device.name: IDS uEye camera (pydcu ueye.camera)

facts.text: The README points the user to the IDS uEye driver package, to /usr/lib/libueye_api.so, and to `from uc480 import pycam`, `camera = pycam()`, `camera.snapshot('some_name.bmp')`
On POSIX the module resolves the vendor library name ueye_api and loads it with ctypes at import time; when find_library returns None the module prints an error and LoadLibrary(None) fails
The module is Python 2 source: line 27 is a print statement and line 40 compares with unicode, so the Python 3 ast parser cannot read the file
class pycam creates a camera(camera_id) and an image wrapper and then allocates and activates image memory
pycam.snapshot captures a frame with IS.WAIT, stops live video with IS.WAIT and calls SaveImage(filename)
class camera wraps the SDK handle and initializes it with is_InitCamera
The camera constructor sets width 1024 and height 768 and allocates a NumPy image buffer; these are constructor defaults, not a sensor limit
SetImageSize reads the current AOI width or height when the x argument has the 0x8000 bit set and returns the queried value, otherwise it sets the size
SetImagePos reads the current AOI x or y position when x has the 0x8000 bit set and returns the queried value, otherwise it sets the position
CaptureVideo digitizes a frame into the image memory allocated by AllocImageMem and activated by SetImageMem; IS.WAIT waits until acquisition begins
StopLiveVideo stops live video; with IS.WAIT it waits until the image is completely acquired
SaveImage writes the active image memory to the named file through is_SaveImage
ExitCamera closes the camera handle through is_ExitCamera
The IS module defines GET_IMAGE_SIZE_X 0x8000 and GET_IMAGE_SIZE_Y 0x8001 for the size queries and GET_IMAGE_POS_X 0x8001 and GET_IMAGE_POS_Y 0x8002 for the position queries
The IS module defines WAIT 0x0001 and DONT_WAIT 0x0000
setup.py installs only the top-level modules ueye and IS and declares no licence
